mcssize.alpha_sweep_invariant.provenance: mcs_size.py::main, set equality over the sweep
mcssize.alpha_sweep_invariant.spec: True when the curated non-identification count takes a SINGLE value across the whole alpha sweep, with PI point-identified throughout. This is the claim §4.1 rests on when it says the headline does not depend on the test's level

mcssize.alpha_sweep_nonidentified.provenance: mcs_size.py::main alpha sweep over the curated per-year absolute-loss panels
mcssize.alpha_sweep_nonidentified.spec: Curated-panel non-identification count at the STRICTEST alpha swept (0.001, vs the paper's nominal 0.10). Note: a stricter alpha eliminates LESS readily, so the surviving (non-identified) set can mechanically only STAY THE SAME OR GROW as alpha shrinks, never shrink. An unchanged count here is therefore expected regardless of whether mcssize.size_at_nominal_10's over-rejection is real, and does NOT by itself rule out that the nominal-alpha=0.10 count is size-inflated. What it DOES show, together with mcssize.alpha_sweep_invariant: relaxing elimination all the way to alpha=0.001 does not reverse or shrink the finding -- i.e. the headline is not an artifact of a specific, aggressive choice of alpha

cites: S4.2 body: empirical size at the nominal alpha
mcssize.oversize_ratio.cross_check: round(mcssize.size_at_nominal_10 / 0.10, 1) -- the raw quotient is 2.65, and Python's round-half-to-even takes it to 2.6, not 2.7
mcssize.oversize_ratio.spec: mcssize.size_at_nominal_10 divided by the nominal alpha=0.10, i.e. how many times oversized the elimination rule's empirical size is at these panel dimensions

cites: S4.2 body: empirical size at the nominal alpha
mcssize.size_ar1_at_nominal_10.spec: Empirical rejection rate of the first-step equal-predictive-ability null on EXACTLY-NULL panels whose loss series each follow an AR(1) with the panel's own pooled lag-1 differential autocorrelation (phi=0.25, election.ar1null_coefficient), at the paper's K/T/block and nominal alpha=0.10. The i.i.d. figure (mcssize.size_at_nominal_10, in the `iid` field) understates the operating size under the serial dependence the losses actually carry; the direction is the same (sets too small, non-identification counts a lower bound, Section 7's model channel understated)

mcssize.size_arch.spec: The SAME level measured through arch 8.0.0's independent implementation of the Hansen-Lunde-Nason range statistic on IDENTICAL null panels. Its agreement with mcssize.size_at_nominal_10 is what establishes the size distortion as a property of the statistic at these panel dimensions rather than a defect in this repository

mcssize.size_at_K10.spec: Same empirical-size measurement as mcssize.size_at_nominal_10, at K=10 models instead of the paper's K=6, holding T/block fixed -- the K-grows leg of the finite-sample pattern

mcssize.size_at_T400.spec: Same empirical-size measurement as mcssize.size_at_nominal_10, at 4x the paper's panel length (T=400 vs T=30), holding K/block fixed -- the T-shrinks leg of the finite-sample pattern

mcssize.size_at_block6.spec: Same empirical-size measurement as mcssize.size_at_nominal_10, at double the paper's block length (block=6 vs block=3), holding K/T fixed -- the block-grows leg of the finite-sample pattern

cites: S4.2 body: empirical size at the nominal alpha
mcssize.size_at_nominal_10.spec: Empirical rejection rate of the first-step equal-predictive-ability null (at least one model eliminated) on EXACTLY-NULL iid panels at the paper's own K/T/block, against a nominal level of 0.10. Greater than nominal means the test eliminates too readily, which makes every confidence set in this paper if anything too SMALL and the non-identification count a lower bound

mcssize.size_state_dims.spec: The same first-step size at the dimensions of Section 7's state tie-set test (K=4 candidate models, T=35 annual cells): i.i.d. null in the value, AR(1) phi=0.25 null in the `ar1` field. Quoted where Section 7 says its tie sets come from an oversized test
